summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, alcoholic cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, and chronic pain was admitted for headache, somnolence, and acute kidney injury. She had been taking increased NSAIDs and narcotics for pain, leading to acute tubular necrosis and medication intoxication due to impaired renal clearance. On admission, she had hyperkalemia, treated with kayexalate and insulin, and was found to have muddy brown casts on urinalysis. Her mental status improved with discontinuation of nephrotoxic medications and supportive care. Gabapentin and opioids were held and later restarted at reduced doses. Blood pressure was managed with felodipine after stopping valsartan. She remained afebrile with no evidence of infection despite a low-count urine culture. Her kidney function gradually improved, and she was discharged home with adjusted medications, including reduced doses of gabapentin, ciprofloxacin, and iron, and instructions to avoid NSAIDs and valsartan.
